verdict.rationale: Bitwarden's own docs say vaults can be exported for backup and mention importing from 'encrypted exports', so encrypted backups exist as a first-party capability. Nothing first-party shows the key is never held by the vendor or that the encryption design is documented; only a community comment calls Bitwarden an e2ee password manager. missing for 10: documented end-to-end/zero-knowledge key custody for vault data and exports, published encryption design (KDF, cipher, key hierarchy), independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a security engineer, backups are end-to-end encrypted with a key the vendor never holds, and the encryption design is documented

citations.quote: Export your vault data, including logins and notes, to back up important information or transfer to a new Bitwarden vault.
Import logins and data from different password managers, other Bitwarden vaults, or encrypted exports
Needless to say I move to the next ethical e2ee password manager if BitWarden turns its back on open source.
